task: Find all assays of molecules concerning electrophilic or metabolically activated reactivity and oxidative damage. This includes formation of reactive metabolites, nucleophile or DNA adducts, glutathione depletion, reactive oxygen species, oxidative DNA damage, and lipid peroxidation. Make sure to include assays such as S9-dependent activity, reactive-metabolite trapping, glutathione depletion, DNA adductomics, intracellular ROS, glutathione redox, TBARS or malondialdehyde, 8-oxo-dG, and FPG-modified comet assays. Specify the endpoint and measurement unit, molecule concentration or dose, exposure duration and readout time, assay type, cell or tissue type, species, metabolic activation system, oxygen and media conditions, cytotoxicity, analytical detection method, and antioxidant-rescue or scavenger controls. Include all key experimental details.
task_instantiation:
Create records that answer: which globally identified molecule, reactive metabolite, defined mixture, exposure, or protective intervention shows positive, negative, unchanged, mixed, or equivocal evidence of electrophilic or metabolically activated reactivity, reactive-product/adduct formation, ROS/RNS generation, glutathione perturbation, or oxidative molecular damage; what exact endpoint, assay, and analytical method support the finding; what response and unit were reported; at what molecule concentration or dose, exposure duration, and readout/sample-collection time; in what cell-free, subcellular, cellular, tissue, in-vivo, microbial, or human system, and in what source species; whether exogenous metabolic activation was present and what S9, microsomal/NADPH, recombinant-enzyme, peroxidase, cellular, in-vivo, chemical, photochemical, or other activation context was used; and whether oxygen/media conditions, cytotoxicity, antioxidants, nucleophiles, scavengers, chelators, inhibitors, depletion/repletion, or rescue controls qualify the interpretation.

IN SCOPE. Extract experimentally performed assays that directly measure: (1) electrophile–nucleophile reaction, kinetics, peptide/GSH depletion, or defined reactive-species scavenging; (2) reactive/electrophilic metabolite or radical formation, trapping, or experimentally supported mechanism-based enzyme inactivation; (3) GSH, cysteine, NAC, cyanide, semicarbazide, peptide, protein, lipid, RNA, DNA, or other covalent adducts, covalent binding, targeted adduct analysis, DNA adductomics, or mercapturic products explicitly used as reactive-electrophile evidence; (4) GSH or non-protein-thiol depletion, GSSG, GSH/GSSG or related glutathione redox, protein S-glutathionylation, or direct protein-thiol oxidation; (5) intracellular, mitochondrial, extracellular, microsomal, tissue, biofluid, or cell-free ROS/RNS, specific radicals/peroxides, spin trapping, or redox cycling/oxygen uptake explicitly interpreted as reactive-species production; (6) oxidative DNA lesions such as 8-oxo-dG/8-OHdG and FPG-, hOGG1-, EndoIII-, or other lesion-enzyme-modified comet endpoints; (7) lipid peroxidation measured by TBARS/MDA, 4-HNE or related aldehydes/adducts, lipid hydroperoxides, isoprostanes, conjugated dienes, volatile hydrocarbons, oxidized lipids, or C11-BODIPY-like probes; (8) direct oxidative protein damage such as carbonyls, oxidized thiols, nitrotyrosine, or defined oxidative/electrophile-protein adducts; and (9) Ames, mutation, comet, cytotoxic, or other activity whose evidentiary feature is an explicit with-versus-without S9 or other metabolic-activation comparison. Include explicit negative, not-detected, unchanged, weak, mixed, and equivocal assay findings. Include a protective molecule when its effect is measured through an in-scope endpoint. Include standalone scavenging only when it directly quantifies disappearance or inhibition of a named radical, oxidant, reactive carbonyl, electrophile, or in-scope molecular-damage endpoint.

EXCLUDE. Exclude ordinary metabolic stability, clearance, parent depletion, or stable-metabolite identification unless a product is explicitly reactive/electrophilic, trapped, covalently bound, or linked to a qualifying activation-dependent endpoint. Exclude generic cytotoxicity, viability, LDH, apoptosis, necrosis, ATP, mitochondrial membrane potential, histology, inflammation, organ-injury biomarkers, lipid accumulation, signaling, Nrf2/HO-1, gene/protein expression, and standalone SOD, catalase, GPx, GR, GST, CYP, or other enzyme activity. These may be retained only as context for an in-scope endpoint from the same arm. Exclude generic antioxidant-capacity screens such as DPPH, ABTS, FRAP, or TOSC unless they directly quantify a defined in-scope reactive species or damage endpoint. Exclude generic mutation, micronucleus, chromosome aberration, unmodified comet, DNA fragmentation, γ-H2AX, or strand breaks unless oxidative-lesion specificity, reactive-metabolite/adduct evidence, or explicit metabolic-activation dependence is established. Exclude disease-only biomarker differences without a named molecule exposure or intervention, ordinary NO/nitrite alone, computational alerts or predictions, proposed pathways, narrative mechanisms, unsupported review conclusions, probe/kit listings, standard preparation alone, and methods-only passages without an explicit assay outcome.

RECORD GRANULARITY. One record is one global_identifier/primary entity × broad endpoint category × exact endpoint × assay/analytical method × biological system/species × exogenous-activation arm × molecule dose/concentration × exposure duration × readout time. Split whenever any of these dimensions has a separately reported result: different molecules or attributable mixture constituents; GSH, GSSG, and a redox ratio; ROS species; distinct damage endpoints or individually quantified adducts; different assay methods; species, tissues, cell lines, or fractions; +activation and −activation arms; materially different oxygen/media conditions; doses; exposure durations; or readout times. Merge technical replicates and repeated descriptions. If only an aggregate dose-response, time-course trend, threshold, range, or untargeted panel is reported, keep one record and preserve the complete range or panel; do not invent point-specific values. For identification-only adductomics or trapping under one condition, one record may list multiple products; split products only when separately quantified. Keep an inseparable mixture as one record unless component-specific outcomes are reported.

The primary entity is the supplied global_identifier. Do not substitute GSH, ROS, MDA, 8-oxo-dG, a probe, enzyme, trap, standard, or measured adduct for the tested entity unless that substance itself is the represented test entity. In a rescue experiment, center the record on global_identifier: if it identifies the protectant, record the protectant's modification of the endpoint and name the damaging challenge in extra_details; otherwise retain the damaging/test molecule and describe the rescuer there.

EVIDENCE THRESHOLD. Require an explicit numerical value, detected/not-detected statement, increase/decrease/no-change statement, binary activity call, or clearly described experimental outcome. Methods may supply conditions for a linked result elsewhere in the supplied paper text, but methods alone do not qualify. A cited prior experiment may be extracted only when the text supplies a concrete assay identity, outcome, and enough system information to reconstruct the record; label it as cited prior evidence in extra_details. Exclude speculation and review-level synthesis without recoverable experiment-level evidence. Do not infer a reactive metabolite merely because a metabolite formed; oxidative comet specificity from an ordinary comet result; TBARS from MDA unless stated; metabolic activation from an intact cell, hepatocyte, or in-vivo system unless metabolism is part of the reported design or interpretation; or an assay platform from field convention.

NORMALIZATION AND NULLS. Preserve reported values, ranges, units, times, doses, and wavelengths without conversion or recalculation. Normalize only unambiguous lexical synonyms and species names. Do not infer species, cell origin, activation enzyme, dose, unit, assay chemistry, oxygen level, cytotoxicity status, or significance. Every field is nullable. Use null—not unspecified, not stated, not reported, not applicable, unclear, none, or similar placeholders—when the paper does not supply information. An explicitly compared no-activation arm, or a clearly defined direct chemical arm with no added metabolism, must be written out in metabolic_activation_system as that arm; null there means the status was not established, not that activation was absent.

DEFAULT CONDITIONS. Treat routine air-equilibrated cell-free buffer, routine normoxic mammalian culture at approximately 37 °C in the paper's standard medium, ordinary in-vivo physiology/husbandry, and conventional untreated/vehicle controls only as defaults for recognizing exceptional conditions. Never populate an unreported default. Record explicitly stated or chemistry-relevant departures—hypoxia, hyperoxia, anaerobiosis, gas composition, unusual pH, buffer, medium, serum, temperature, light, solvent, cofactors, closed systems, disease/genotype, diet, induction, knockdown, or pretreatment—in extra_details.

FIELD USE AND SPILL RULES. assay_and_detection_method must identify both the experimental format and the analytical readout when stated, without guessing. endpoint must name the exact analyte, lesion, adduct, reactive species, target, or mutation readout. reported_result must preserve direction, magnitude, comparator, uncertainty, range, fold/percent change, detection wording, or compact dose/time mapping; every numeric response must use a separate measurement_unit. exposure_and_readout_timing must label exposure/incubation duration separately from delayed readout or collection time. biological_system must include the cell line, primary cell, organoid, tissue, biofluid, fraction, organ preparation, microbial strain, or animal/human setting; species carries the normalized source organism and is populated only from an explicit statement or an unambiguous species-bearing system name. metabolic_activation_system must capture exact fractions, enzymes, cofactors, +/−S9 or +/−NADPH design, and explicitly reported dependence, and owns the presence axis: there is no separate activation boolean.

Use extra_details for: paper-specific entity aliases and molecule role; evidence provenance; route and repeated schedule; comparator identities and values not compactly represented in reported_result; named reactive products, proposed-versus-detected status, trapping partners, target residues, adduct structures, and secondary molecules; oxygen, atmosphere, medium, buffer, pH, serum, temperature, light, and solvent; cytotoxicity or assay interference and whether the endpoint occurs below, with, or only at cytotoxic exposure; antioxidant, nucleophile, scavenger, chelator, enzyme inhibitor/inducer, GSH depletion/repletion, rescue, challenge, and co-exposure identities, doses, timing, and outcomes; strain, sex, age, disease/genotype, diet, unusual pretreatment, sample preparation, instrument settings, replicates, uncertainty, statistics, and ancillary non-scope measurements. Do not use extra_details to create standalone records for excluded endpoints.

schema_spec.name: endpoint_category
schema_spec.description: Broad, mutually exclusive mechanistic class of the measured endpoint. Choose one class, then put the exact subtype/readout in endpoint. This field never names an assay format or platform; that belongs in assay_and_detection_method. Priority rules prevent overlap: use direct_electrophile_nucleophile_reactivity only for cell-free in-chemico reaction, kinetics, or nucleophile/peptide depletion, never for glutathione loss inside cells or tissue, which is glutathione_depletion; use reactive_metabolite_trapping when an activation-generated species is revealed through a trapping product; use reactive_metabolite_formation when a reactive product is directly characterized without trapping as the defining format, including mechanism-based enzyme inactivation whose evidence is reactive-metabolite formation; use covalent_adduct_or_binding for direct adduct/binding measurements, including inactivation evidenced by covalent adduction, when not primarily an activation-and-trap experiment; use metabolism_dependent_activity only when the qualifying evidence is activation-dependent activity without a more direct in-scope molecular endpoint. Use defined_reactive_species_scavenging only for direct disappearance/inhibition of a defined species, not for rescue of another category. Use other_direct_reactivity_or_oxidative_damage only when the endpoint is clearly in scope but fits no listed class, and record the paper's own class wording in extra_details. Null if the class cannot be established; placeholder values were dropped.

schema_spec.name: assay_and_detection_method
schema_spec.description: Specific experimental assay format and analytical detection method as reported, for example `GSH trapping in NADPH-fortified human liver microsomes; LC-MS/MS`, `FPG-modified comet; fluorescence microscopy`, `intracellular DCFH-DA; flow cytometry`, or `TBARS; absorbance at 532 nm`. Include named guideline/strain, probe, chromatography, MS, radiometric, immunochemical, microscopy, EPR/ESR, or spectroscopic method needed to identify the readout. Do not guess a method from the endpoint, and do not restate the endpoint_category class label here. Null when not stated; do not emit a placeholder.

schema_spec.name: endpoint
schema_spec.description: Exact single measured endpoint, subtype, analyte, lesion, reactive species, adduct/product, target, mutation readout, or kinetic quantity, using the paper's terminology—for example GSH depletion RC50, APAP-GSH conjugate, protein-bound radioactivity, S9-dependent TA98 revertants, superoxide-specific 2-hydroxyethidium, GSH/GSSG ratio, FPG-sensitive tail intensity, 8-oxo-dG/dG, MDA, C11-BODIPY oxidation, or protein carbonyl content. This is the subtype layer beneath endpoint_category. Include concise trap/target identity when it defines the endpoint; put structural or site detail in extra_details. Null only when no exact endpoint can be identified; missingness is never encoded as a value.

schema_spec.name: effect_direction
schema_spec.description: Mutually exclusive form/direction of the reported result. Use detected/not_detected only for presence or identification assays; increased/decreased/unchanged for comparative quantities; positive_call/negative_call only for an explicitly binary assay call such as activation-dependent mutagenicity; absolute_or_kinetic_measurement for an absolute level, rate, or kinetic constant without a directional comparison; mixed for genuinely opposing unsplittable directions; and equivocal when the reported outcome is inconclusive or borderline and no stable direction can be assigned. Protective inhibition is normally decreased and enhancement is increased for the measured endpoint. Null if no direction or result form is stated. Placeholder values were dropped.

schema_spec.name: reported_result
schema_spec.description: Exact concise result as reported, excluding the measurement unit: central value, mean ± uncertainty, inequality, range, ratio, fold/percent change, detection-limit wording, qualitative conclusion, comparator, significance, or compact dose/time-to-result mapping for an unsplit aggregate trend. Do not calculate unreported changes or convert values. If a numerical result is present, measurement_unit must separately contain its unit or normalization basis. Null when the paper supplies only effect_direction and no further result text; do not use a missing-information placeholder.

schema_spec.name: measurement_unit
schema_spec.description: Unit and normalization basis applying to numerical content in reported_result, exactly as reported and without conversion, such as `nmol/mg protein`, `% tail DNA`, `adducts/10^8 nucleotides`, `relative fluorescence units`, `fold over control`, `M^-1 s^-1`, or `dimensionless ratio`. For multiple inseparable values, list corresponding units only if unambiguous. Null for a purely qualitative result or when the paper gives no unit; do not encode qualitative, unitless-by-assumption, not reported, or not applicable as values.

schema_spec.name: molecule_concentration_or_dose
schema_spec.description: Concentration or administered dose of the global_identifier entity, preserving the reported value, range, formulation basis, unit, and inseparable frequency information without conversion. Include several levels only for an aggregate series lacking separable point results. Do not substitute the dose of a probe, substrate, trapping agent, challenge, standard, or rescuer; put those in extra_details. Null if absent rather than using a placeholder.

schema_spec.name: exposure_and_readout_timing
schema_spec.description: Labeled timing for this record, preserving reported units and sequence: `exposure/incubation duration: ...; readout/sample-collection time: ...`. Include pretreatment, challenge, washout, recovery, repeated-treatment period, or delayed sacrifice when they define the arm. Do not duplicate exposure duration as readout time merely because measurement occurred at exposure end unless the paper explicitly states both. Either component may be omitted within the string if not reported; the whole field is null when no timing is supplied. Never write a missing-information placeholder.

schema_spec.name: biological_system
schema_spec.description: Concise description of the experimental system in which the endpoint was measured, excluding the organism identity, which goes in species: cell-free matrix or reaction mixture; purified/recombinant system; microsomes, mitochondria, cytosol, S9 or other fraction; cell line or primary cell; organoid; tissue, slice, isolated organ, biofluid, or whole animal; microbial strain; or human observational/clinical sample. Keep the paper's designation intact even when it embeds an organism word (`human liver microsomes`, `primary rat hepatocytes`); species then repeats that organism in normalized form. For a purely chemical assay, describe the chemical matrix; do not encode not applicable. Null if the system is not stated.

schema_spec.name: species
schema_spec.description: Source organism of the biological material in which the endpoint was measured, normalized to a single scientific or unambiguous common name as stated by the paper, for example `Homo sapiens`, `Rattus norvegicus`, `Mus musculus`, or `Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium`. Take it only from an explicit statement or an unambiguous species-bearing system name in biological_system; do not infer species from an ambiguous cell-line designation, from a supplier, or from field convention. Put strain, sex, age, and genotype in extra_details. Null for a purely chemical cell-free system with no biological material and whenever the organism is not established; never write not applicable or another placeholder.

schema_spec.name: metabolic_activation_system
schema_spec.description: Exact reported metabolic or chemical activation arm for this record, covering both whether activation was present and what it was: source/species/tissue of S9, microsomes, cytosol, recombinant CYP or other enzyme, peroxidase, beta-lyase, intact-cell or in-vivo metabolism, cofactors such as NADPH or an NADPH-generating system, heat-inactivation or inhibitor controls, chemical/metal/redox activation, photochemical activation, and any explicit required/not-required or enhanced/no-effect dependence statement — for example `rat liver S9 plus NADPH-generating system; activity seen only with S9`, `NADPH-fortified human liver microsomes`, `recombinant CYP3A4`, or `without S9`. An explicitly compared no-activation arm, or a defined direct chemical reaction with no added metabolism, must be written out as that arm (`without S9`, `no exogenous activation, direct chemical reaction`) rather than left null. Record intact-cell, hepatocyte, liver, or in-vivo metabolism only when it is part of the reported design or interpretation, never inferred from the system alone; do not name an unreported enzyme. Null means the activation status was not established, which is not the same as absent; all not-stated placeholders were dropped.

schema_spec.name: extra_details
schema_spec.description: Additional non-core details that do not fit above. Record, when reported and relevant: paper aliases and the primary entity's role; cited-prior-evidence status; route and regimen; comparators; named reactive products, traps, targets, adduct structures/sites, and proposed-versus-detected nuance; challenge/co-exposure molecules; oxygen, atmosphere, medium, buffer, pH, serum, temperature, light, solvent, and unusual cofactors; cytotoxicity, viability, or assay interference needed to interpret the in-scope endpoint; antioxidant, scavenger, nucleophile, chelator, metabolic inhibitor/inducer, GSH manipulation, and rescue-control identities, doses, timing, and outcomes; strain, sex, age, disease/genotype, diet, pretreatment, sample preparation, instrument settings, replicates, uncertainty, statistics, and ancillary findings. Do not use this field to create standalone excluded endpoints. Use null, never a placeholder, when there are no extra details.
